question: When does Statutory Sick Pay start being paid?
prompt:
You are an assistant answering questions about an organisation's internal policies and procedures.

Rules:

EVIDENCE:
[HR-12#002] Sickness Absence Policy > Certification; Sick pay (v3.0, effective 2026-04-06)
| Absence length | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 1 to 7 calendar days | Self-certification form on return |
| 8 calendar days or more | Fit note from a GP, provided within 5 days |

Statutory Sick Pay is payable from the first qualifying day of absence. There are no longer any unpaid waiting days.

All employees qualify for Statutory Sick Pay regardless of their earnings. The Lower Earnings Limit no longer applies to sick pay, so part-time and lower-paid staff who were previously excluded are now covered.

Statutory Sick Pay is paid at the lower of the statutory weekly rate or 80 per cent of the employee's average weekly earnings. The statutory weekly rate for 2026/27 is £123.25.

Fire wardens take a roll call at the assembly point using the daily attendance list and the visitor book from reception. Managers must account for their team and report to the senior warden.

Anyone who has left site during the day but not signed out will be reported as unaccounted for, so signing out matters.

---

[OPS-07#003] Fire Evacuation Procedure > Assembly point (v3.0, effective 2026-01-01)
The assembly point is the north corner of the staff car park, beside the blue container.

Do not re-enter the building for any reason until a fire warden confirms it is safe.

---

The site has six trained fire wardens, identified by yellow high-visibility tabards kept at each fire point. Warden training is refreshed every two years.

Fire extinguishers are inspected annually by a competent contractor. The alarm is tested every Wednesday at 10:00; this is a short test and does not require evacuation.

A full evacuation drill is held twice per year.

Any employee may stop a task they believe to be unsafe without fear of consequence. Report the concern to the supervisor immediately.

question: How quickly must a suspected data breach be reported?
prompt:

Rules:

A suspected personal data breach is reported to the Data Protection Lead within 24 hours of discovery, whether or not it is later confirmed.

Access to systems holding personal data is reviewed annually by the Data Protection Lead. Managers confirm in writing that every account in their area is still required.

---

[IT-03#002] Security Incident Reporting > How to report; Timescales (v1.6, effective 2025-11-01)
Telephone the IT helpdesk on extension 4040 immediately, and follow up by email to ithelp@northgate-kitchenware.invalid. Do not attempt to fix or investigate the problem yourself, and do not delete anything, as evidence may be needed.

|---|---|
| Report to IT helpdesk | Within 1 hour of becoming aware |
| IT initial assessment | Within 4 hours |
| Notify Data Protection Lead if personal data is involved | Within 24 hours |
| Notify the ICO if the breach is likely to risk individuals' rights | Within 72 hours of the company becoming aware |
| Notify affected individuals if the risk is high | Without undue delay |

---

[IT-03#001] Security Incident Reporting > What counts as an incident (v1.6, effective 2025-11-01)
Report any of the following:

- A lost or stolen laptop, phone or USB device
- An email sent to the wrong recipient containing personal or confidential data
- Clicking a link or opening an attachment in a suspected phishing email
- Suspected malware, ransomware or unexpected system behaviour
- Unauthorised access to a system, room or filing cabinet
- Paper records lost, or found where they should not be
- Any suspicion that a password has been compromised

If you are unsure whether something is an incident, report it. Reporting something harmless costs a few minutes; not reporting a real breach can cost the company a great deal more.

---

Suspected breaches of this schedule, including data retained past its period or disposed of early, are reported to the Data Protection Lead within 72 hours.

At the end of the retention period, electronic records are deleted, including from backups at the next backup cycle rollover, and paper records are cross-cut shredded. Disposal of confidential waste is carried out under a certificate of destruction.

Deletion is not performed where a record is subject to an ongoing legal claim, investigation or regulatory request. In that case the record is placed on legal hold and the reason recorded.

The Data Protection Lead reviews this schedule annually against current legislation.

prompt:

[OPS-06#002] Forklift Truck Operations > Pre-use inspection (v1.8, effective 2025-07-01)
A documented pre-use check is completed at the start of every shift, before the truck is used, covering:

- Tyres, forks and mast for damage
- Hydraulic leaks
- Brakes, including the parking brake
- Horn, lights and beacon
- Battery charge and electrolyte level where applicable
- Seat belt condition and operation

Defects are recorded on the daily check sheet. A truck with a safety-critical defect is taken out of service, the key removed, and a "do not use" tag applied. Report to the Warehouse Supervisor immediately.

---

[OPS-06#004] Forklift Truck Operations > End of shift; Statutory inspection (v1.8, effective 2025-07-01)
Park in the designated bay, lower the forks fully, apply the parking brake, switch off, remove the key and return it to the key cabinet. Trucks on charge must have the charging area kept clear and ventilated.

Every truck receives a thorough examination under LOLER 1998. The interval is 12 months for trucks used only to lift loads, and 6 months for any truck fitted with a working platform or man-riding cage, because equipment used to lift people must be examined at the shorter interval. The two counterbalance trucks certified for use with the man-riding cage referred to in OPS-05 are therefore on the 6-month cycle. Certificates are held in the warehouse office.

- The seat belt must be worn at all times while the truck is in motion
- Maximum speed inside the building is 4 km/h
- Travel with the forks lowered approximately 100 mm from the floor and the mast tilted back
- Travel in reverse when the load obstructs forward vision
- Never lift or carry a passenger
- Never leave a truck unattended with the forks raised or the engine running
- Sound the horn at aisle ends, blind corners and the goods-in door

Damage reports are acknowledged within two working days of being received.
